reason: The cited evidence supports that slow cooling leads to a complex crystalline microstructure (E3) and that rapid cooling yields an amorphous structure (E1, E2, E3), with phosphorus enhancing glass-forming ability (E1, E2). However, the premises that localized remelting can dissolve crystals and that ultrafast quenching after remelting can suppress re-nucleation are not directly supported by the cited passages, which only describe bulk cooling methods and do not address laser remelting or its effects.
premises: Slow cooling produces a complex multiphase crystalline microstructure in the alloy
Rapid cooling (10^5–10^6 K/s) yields an amorphous structure
Phosphorus enhances glass-forming ability during rapid cooling
Localized remelting can dissolve preformed crystals and reset microstructure
Ultrafast quenching after remelting can suppress re-nucleation and retain amorphous phase
